question: Braking is more effective when you depress the brake pedal

options.text: With the gear engaged.
With the clutch depressed.
With the gear lever in 'Neutral'.

question: A lower gear has

options.text: More power and less speed than a higher gear.
More speed and less power than a higher gear.
Less power and less speed than a higher gear.

question: After engaging the first gear and the clutch pedal is released to the 'biting point', there is

options.text: A slight drop in the engine revolution.
A slight increase in the engine revolution.
No change in the engine revolution.

question: At a sharp bend you should

options.text: Not overtake other vehicles.
Overtake, if the speed of the vehicle in front is slow.
Follow closely behind the front car.

question: After parking your car on an upward slope, you should

options.text: Engage the 1st gear.
Engage the reverse gear.
Shift the gear to neutral.

question: When two vehicles moving in opposite directions meet on a slope where the road is narrow, which vehicle should give way?

options.text: The vehicle that is going up slope.
The vehicle that is going down slope.
The smaller vehicle.

question: If a motorcyclist is trying to overtake you, you should

options.text: Drive faster to prevent the rider from overtaking you.
Slow down and assist the rider to overtaking safely.
Signal the driver to overtake on the left.

notes: Source grammar in option B: 'assist the rider to overtaking safely' (kept as printed). Option C says 'driver' although the question is about a motorcyclist.

question: Before reversing, you should check

options.text: Behind.
All round.
Ahead and behind.

question: Before you reverse, you must make sure that there are no

options.text: Other vehicles behind you.
Children, pedestrian and obstruction in the blind area.
Both answers above.

notes: Source grammar in option B: 'pedestrian and obstruction' singular (kept as printed).

question: On rainy day, less tread on your tyres will

options.text: Increase your braking distance.
Decrease your braking distance.
Not affect your braking distance.

notes: Source grammar in question: 'On rainy day' (missing 'a'), kept as printed.

question: Under inflated tyres will make the steering feel

options.text: Light.
Heavy.
Normal.

question: If you increase your speed when going round a bend, it will be

options.text: Difficult for you to keep your intended path.
Safer for you.
Easier for you to control your car.

question: The stopping distance on a wet road is _____ longer than on a dry road.

options.text: 4 times
3 times
2 times

notes: Question contains a fill-in blank drawn as an underline; exact underscore count approximated as five. Options have no final full stop.

question: In an emergency stop, you should

options.text: Apply only the brakes.
Apply the brakes and clutch together.
Apply the clutch first and then the brakes.

question: On a sharp bend at night, to avoid dazzling oncoming traffic, you should

options.text: Switch off your lights.
Dip your headlights.
Swith on high beam.

notes: Source typo in option C: 'Swith' (should be 'Switch'), kept as printed.

question: The purpose of using dipped headlights whilst driving is to

options.text: To save the battery's electrical energy.
To light up the road immediately in front of you.
To avoid dazzling drivers of oncoming vehicles.

question: When following a car driven by an elderly driver, you should

options.text: Flash your lights and overtake.
Be aware that the driver's reactions may not be as fast as yours.
Expect the driver to drive badly.

question: When the traffic light turns green at a junction, you should

options.text: Depress the accelerator hard and move off quickly.
Check traffic from right and left before moving off.
Only move off when other vehicles move.

question: When you see a vehicle slowing down at a pedestrian crossing, you should

options.text: Overtake the slow moving vehicle.
Maintain your normal speed.
Slow down and be ready to stop.

question: Before overtaking a large vehicle you should keep a longer distance. The reason is

options.text: To offer others a gap if they wanted to overtake you.
To get the best view of the road ahead.
To leave a gap in case the vehicle stops abruptly and rolls back.
